note: MET exon 14 skipping was found in patients and shown crizotinib-sensitive first (2015, a non-member), but the member drugs' own MET-driven xenografts prospectively set the tumour phospho-MET exposure target and the METex14/high-level-amplification population that GEOMETRY and VISION confirmed, while animal toxicology caught liver and pancreas harms and, for capmatinib, missed the class's signature peripheral oedema.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the S114 phospho-MET dose-response (>=0.3 mg/kg ~90% inhibition) is quoted from the FDA capmatinib review, which re-describes Liu 2011.

engagement.quote: This inhibitor potently blocks c-MET phosphorylation and activation of its key downstream effectors in c-MET-dependent tumor cell lines.

engagement.magnitude_basis: fractional tumour phospho-MET inhibition (~90% at >=0.3 mg/kg in S114 allografts vs 95% in patient biopsies)

engagement.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
engagement.note: Phase 1 tumour biopsies: 95% phospho-MET inhibition in two NSCLC patients and near-complete in one at the RP2D, matching the mouse S114 target. Dated 2019: Bang 2020 (10.1111/cas.14254, epub 2019-12-30) first put the biopsy phospho-MET result beside the mouse target (earliest public date).
engagement.quote: Pharmacodynamic data showed that 1 subject (with advanced colorectal cancer) had near-complete phospho-MET inhibition at 450 mg b.i.d. with capsules, and 2 subjects with NSCLC in the expansion phase had phosphorylated MET inhibition of 95%.
engagement.judgement: Tumour phospho-MET is the kinase's own autophosphorylation, so it is scored proximal rather than direct (no occupancy or free-target assay exists). Comparison counted as stated because the review places the clinical phospho-MET data beside the S114-derived IC95.

engagement.short: Tepotinib biopsies fit xenograft phospho-MET model

engagement.reason: Patient tumour phospho-MET matched xenograft target
engagement.judgement: Strengthens, not a new status: a second member drug with human tumour phospho-MET read against the same xenograft PD readout.

engagement.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
engagement.note: Tepotinib (EMD 1214063) cut c-MET phosphorylation dose-dependently in xenografts; no human tumour phospho-MET yet.
engagement.quote: Both EMD 1214063 and EMD 1204831 inhibited c-Met phosphorylation and downstream signaling in a dose-dependent fashion, but differed in the duration of their inhibitory activity.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry of the tepotinib track at the xenograft system's first use for tepotinib.

dose.confidence_note: Exposure-efficacy was flat within the single dose level, so 'enough' rests on the cohort ORR, not on a dose-response.
dose.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
dose.note: Human IC95 (132 ng/mL) derived from S114 allograft PK/PD; 400 mg BID keeps 96% of patients above it, MTD not reached, ORR 41-68%.

dose.quote: Based on population PK simulations, 96% (90% CI: 94%, 98%) of patients have steady state capmatinib plasma concentration above IC95 for MET inhibition during the dosing interval with 400 mg b.i.d regimen.
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the model stated the effective exposure was tolerated (Liu 2011) and the clinic reached it without that toxicity (MTD not reached at 600 mg BID capsules), so margin_stated is true. Dose is scored same because efficacy was positive at that exposure.

dose.magnitude_basis: simulated tumour phospho-MET inhibition at 500 mg vs the >=95% regression threshold from KP-4 xenografts
dose.population: MET exon 14 skipping NSCLC (VISION cohort A)
dose.confidence_note: Quote is a verbatim sub-span of the FDA's assessment sentence; Falchook 2020 gives the same RP2D rationale (abstract read).
dose.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
dose.note: Tepotinib 500 mg once daily chosen to give >=95% tumour phospho-MET inhibition from xenograft PK/PD; MTD not reached up to 1400 mg; VISION ORR 46%. Dated 2019: Falchook 2020 (epub 2019-12-10) first published the 500 mg rationale from the xenograft target with MTD not reached (earliest public date).
dose.quote: this dosing regimen with food could achieve ≥ 95% phospho-MET inhibition in tumors in greater than 90% of the population
dose.reason: Xenograft phospho-MET target reached and sufficient

The rat 26-week study could not reach human AUC (0.04-0.13x), so the toxicology margin, as distinct from the mouse efficacy margin, is thin.

dose.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials

dose.judgement: A dose prediction exists (lower savolitinib dose equivalent) but no trial has tested it, so untested rather than an empty cell.

efficacy.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice

efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft regression vs 18% ORR in MET-amplified NSCLC
efficacy.confidence_note: Phase 1 whose primary endpoint was MTD; preliminary efficacy in the amplification-selected expansion was a stated objective, scored as the proof-of-concept gate. No correlation of response with gene copy number. The phase 2 NCT02435121 (start 2015-11) posted no results; registry results date absent for both trials. Abstract-level reading of both papers.
efficacy.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
efficacy.note: SAR125844: MET-amplified xenografts (SNU-5, Hs746T) predicted amplification-selected activity; 4/22 MET-amplified NSCLC responded, none with high p-MET only. Retrodiction: the SAR125844 xenografts (Egile, epub 2014-12-10) were public after crizotinib, a MET inhibitor, had produced responses in MET-amplified NSCLC (Ou 2011 case report; Camidge ASCO 2014), so the reproduced result scores retro. Phase 1 expansion scored on its stated preliminary-efficacy objective.
efficacy.quote: Of the 29 evaluable patients with MET amplification treated at 570 mg/m2, five achieved a partial response, including four of 22 with NSCLC; 17 patients had stable disease.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same with partial because the amplification-selected prediction held in direction (responses only in MET-amplified tumours) but at 18%, and Sanofi stopped the programme without a reported failure. A stricter reading leaves this untested and starts the strip at GEOMETRY 2020.

patient_trials.quote: No response was observed in patients with high p-MET solid tumours.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PDX partial regressions (65-96%) and LU5381 METex14 PDX growth inhibition vs BIRC ORR 41-68%
efficacy.population: MET exon 14 skipping (cohorts 4, 5b) and MET-amplified (cohorts 1-3, 5a) NSCLC
efficacy.confidence_note: NEJM abstract and the FDA review's nonclinical section read; Baltschukat 2019 abstract only (epub 2019-01-23, after the 2018 ASCO interim but before the NEJM paper). The FDA label (2020-05-06) is the earliest public record of the same trial.
efficacy.model: MET-driven human tumour xenografts/PDX (METex14, high-level MET-amplified) and HGF/MET allografts in mice
efficacy.note: GEOMETRY mono-1: ORR 41% pretreated, 68% naive in METex14; high-level amplification (GCN>=10) 29-40%, GCN<10 cohorts futile, as the high-GCN PDX implied. Retrodiction: the METex14 PDX (Baltschukat, epub 2019-01-23) were public after crizotinib METex14 responses (2015) and capmatinib's own congress interim, so retro; dated 2019, when both halves were public, before the 2020 label and NEJM paper. Single-arm trial scored on its primary endpoint (ORR).
efficacy.quote: Capmatinib showed substantial antitumor activity in patients with advanced NSCLC with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation, particularly in those not treated previously.
efficacy.judgement: Comparison is paired: NEJM does not juxtapose the xenografts; the FDA review does ('These studies support ... its activity in the proposed patient population') but tier 1 sets the status. Partial because the model's amplification call was made on PDX with GCN up to 31 and the GCN<10 cohorts (ORR 7-12%) closed for futility; the model never claimed low-level amplification. The METex14 population was first defined on crizotinib responders (Paik 2015, 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-14-1467; not a member), so the genotype itself is a clinical discovery; the member drugs' xenografts then predicted their own activity in it. Tepotinib (VISION), savolitinib and gumarontinib are listed in patient_trials and change no status.

patient_trials.quote: Among patients with advanced NSCLC with a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation, the use of tepotinib was associated with a partial response in approximately half the patients.
Savolitinib yielded promising activity and had an acceptable safety profile in patients with pulmonary sarcomatoid carcinoma and other NSCLC subtypes positive for METex14 skipping alterations.
The objective response rate was 66% (95% CI 54-76) overall (n = 79), 71% (95% CI 55-83) in treatment-naïve patients (n = 44), and 60% (95% CI 42-76) in previously-treated patients (n = 35).

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.population: Ba/F3 cells transformed with TPR-MET wild-type or D1228V; 293T MET signalling; PC9 derivatives
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC author manuscript). model_kind is ex_vivo because the enum has no in-vitro cell-line value; the system is an engineered murine pro-B line, not patient cells.
efficacy.note: Ba/F3 cells carrying MET kinase-domain variants first used to ask which MET genotypes lose type I TKI (savolitinib, capmatinib, crizotinib) sensitivity.
efficacy.quote: With several structurally distinct MET inhibitors undergoing development for treatment of NSCLC, it is critical to identify mechanism-based therapies for drug resistance.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the same paper carries the retrodictive comparison, entered separately below.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.magnitude_basis: savolitinib sensitivity of TPR-MET wild-type vs D1228V Ba/F3 cells against one patient's progression on savolitinib + osimertinib with a new D1228V mutation
efficacy.population: EGFR-mutant, MET-amplified NSCLC progressing on osimertinib + savolitinib in TATTON (NCT02143466); n = 1
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Single patient; the D1228V allele was found in the patient first and then engineered into Ba/F3 and 293T cells, so this is a retrodiction. The abstract prints METD1228V with a superscript (quoted here with a space). NCT02143466 has no results posted; savolitinib was given with osimertinib, so the MET-inhibitor resistance is on-target but the response being lost was to a combination.
efficacy.note: Patient's savolitinib + osimertinib resistance mutation D1228V, found by NGS, was modelled: TPR-MET D1228V Ba/F3 cells lost savolitinib sensitivity, reproducing the clinic. Combination: savolitinib was given with osimertinib.
efficacy.short: D1228V savolitinib resistance reproduced in Ba/F3
efficacy.quote: Our in vitro findings demonstrate that MET D1228V induces resistance to type I MET TKIs through impaired drug binding, while sensitivity to type II MET TKIs is maintained.
efficacy.judgement: Scored retro, not same: the clinic already knew the answer (D1228V appeared on savolitinib) before the cells were built (decision 10). The paper's forward prediction, that a type II inhibitor would still work, was tested with cabozantinib, a non-member, so it does not score here. Patient-level because the question is which MET genotype keeps responding.

efficacy.model: Ba/F3 cells engineered with MET kinase-domain variants (TPR-MET D1228V; METex14 with ENU-derived secondary mutations) tested against MET TKIs
efficacy.magnitude_basis: resistance residues named by ENU mutagenesis of Ba/F3 METex14 cells (D1228, Y1230 for type I TKIs) against residues mutated at progression on capmatinib or tepotinib
efficacy.population: METex14 NSCLC progressing on capmatinib or tepotinib (case series and resistance cohorts cited by the source)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Fujino 2019 and Fujino 2022. The 2019 screen's eight TKIs are assumed to include capmatinib and tepotinib (not verifiable from the abstract). Recondo 2020 (10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-19-3608, epub 2020-02-07) reports D1228/Y1230 mutations at progression in 7 of 20 METex14 patients on type I/II MET TKIs but its abstract does not itemise which patients were on member drugs, so the comparison may have been public from 2020; paywalled full text not read.
efficacy.note: ENU mutagenesis of Ba/F3 METex14 (2019) named D1228 and Y1230 as type I resistance sites; both recur at progression on capmatinib and tepotinib. Retrodiction: D1228/Y1230 type I resistance was already known in patients on crizotinib and on savolitinib (Bahcall 2016) before the 2019 screen; efficacy is a target claim, so any MET inhibitor's patient result counts.
efficacy.quote: However, the emergence of acquired resistance to capmatinib/tepotinib is almost inevitable partially due to D1228X or Y1230X secondary mutations of the MET.
efficacy.reason: Predicted resistance residues seen on capmatinib/tepotinib
efficacy.judgement: Rescored retro under the retrodiction rule (and the checker's adjudication): the patient result that counts for an efficacy question is any drug's on the same target, and D1228/Y1230 resistance on type I MET TKIs was public (2016) before the 2019 ENU screen. Direction only: the type II residues it also named cannot be tested by the member drugs, all type I.

efficacy.model: Patient-derived lung cancer organoids from malignant effusions or tissue, drug-sensitivity tested (LCO-DST) to steer the patient's own next-line therapy
efficacy.population: advanced lung cancer, 212 lung cancer organoids from 107 patients, mostly malignant-effusion derived
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). Earlier lung-adenocarcinoma organoid cohorts (Kim 2021, 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-5026) carried no MET-inhibitor case, so the track opens here.

efficacy.short: Effusion-derived lung organoids built for DST
efficacy.quote: Tumor organoids are a potential approach in precision medicine for predicting the clinical response to treatment.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the same paper carries the comparison, entered separately below.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: organoid IC50 of osimertinib + savolitinib vs either monotherapy against the patient's confirmed partial response; two METex14 cases (P-86, P-105) scored as accurate without the drug named in the main text

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. One member-drug case, given as a combination with osimertinib, so the savolitinib contribution is not isolated; the two METex14 cases' drug is in Table S6 (not retrieved) and may be crizotinib rather than a member. Real-world cohort, no registered trial. Cohort-level LCO-DST accuracy (83.3%) is for all targeted and chemotherapy regimens, not MET inhibitors.
efficacy.note: Organoid IC50s picked osimertinib + savolitinib for a MET-amplified EGFR-L858R patient who then had confirmed PR; two METex14 cases also predicted accurately. Combination: savolitinib with osimertinib, scored on the patient's response; the organoid test preceded this patient's treatment, so not a retrodiction.
efficacy.quote: the patient was given with osimertinib plus savolitinib since MET amplification were further confirmed in MSE and LCO via fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), immunofluorescence staining, and IHC (Figures 5C, 5D, and S5B), and achieved confirmed PR
efficacy.reason: Organoid call matched the patient's response
efficacy.judgement: Patient-level, prospective (the organoid test preceded the treatment choice), stated in the source. Scored same on one member-drug patient; a reader who requires the MET inhibitor to be given alone, or more than one patient, would leave this untested.

efficacy.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). Built in 2025, after every member trial it is compared with had read out.
efficacy.note: First QSP model of MET signalling; calibrated on capmatinib, tepotinib and savolitinib cell and xenograft data before any clinical comparison.
efficacy.short: MET QSP model built from preclinical data
efficacy.quote: To our knowledge, our work is the first multiscale QSP investigation of MET dysregulation for translational cancer drug research
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the retrodictive virtual-trial comparison in the same paper is entered separately below.

efficacy.model: Quantitative systems pharmacology model of the MET signalling network with virtual METex14 and MET-amplified NSCLC populations run as virtual clinical trials
efficacy.magnitude_basis: simulated vs reported ORR and waterfall response depth (Figure 6I table; the paper's numbers were not extracted, so no fold is computed)
efficacy.population: METex14 NSCLC (GEOMETRY mono-1, VISION, savolitinib NCT02897479) and MET-amplified NSCLC (GEOMETRY mono-1)
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. Capmatinib, tepotinib and crizotinib clinical responses were the training set for the virtual METex14 population, so only the savolitinib (Lu 2021) and MET-amplified capmatinib comparisons are out of sample; the match is the authors' own, judged on waterfall overlap and ORR.
efficacy.note: Virtual trials reproduced GEOMETRY and VISION ORRs after training, then matched savolitinib's METex14 ORR and capmatinib's lower MET-amplified ORR out of sample.
efficacy.quote: the resulting predicted treatment response can again match the reported clinical data in MET ex14 mutated NSCLC patients
efficacy.judgement: Retro, not same: every trial compared had read out (2020-2021) before the model was built (decision 10). Class-level because the virtual populations ask whether MET TKIs work in METex14 or MET-amplified NSCLC as a whole. The PDO arm of the same paper tested no member drug and reports no patient outcome, so it adds nothing to this track.

Among patients with advanced NSCLC with a confirmed MET exon 14 skipping mutation, the use of tepotinib was associated with a partial response in approximately half the patients.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the track opens on the earliest public animal tolerability statement for a member.
safety.model: Mouse tolerability at efficacious doses; GLP rat and cynomolgus monkey toxicology, 3T3 and mouse UV phototoxicity assays (capmatinib)
safety.note: Mice tolerated fully effective capmatinib doses; GLP rat/monkey toxicology dates are not public.
safety.quote: the inhibitor is well tolerated at doses that achieve complete tumor inhibition

safety.magnitude_basis: incidence of harms predicted vs observed; no animal oedema outside one moribund high-dose animal; photosensitivity 1/334 grade 1 vs a mouse UV-LLNA positive
safety.population: MET exon 14 skipping and MET-amplified NSCLC (GEOMETRY mono-1)
safety.confidence_note: FDA nonclinical executive summary and clinical safety sections grepped, not read end to end; the FDA itself calls the pancreas/liver/kidney findings 'consistent with clinical experience' and kept a photosensitivity warning on the animal data.
safety.model: Mouse tolerability at efficacious doses; GLP rat and cynomolgus monkey toxicology, 3T3 and mouse UV phototoxicity assays (capmatinib)
safety.note: Pancreas, liver, kidney and albumin findings held; animals silent on peripheral oedema (51%, the commonest AE) and ILD; photosensitivity over-called (0.3%).
safety.short: Oedema and ILD unpredicted; photosensitivity over-called
safety.quote: The most frequently reported adverse events were peripheral edema (in 51%) and nausea (in 45%); these events were mostly of grade 1 or 2.
safety.reason: Silent on oedema and ILD; over-called photosensitivity
safety.judgement: Stated predictions (amylase/lipase, ALT/AST, creatinine, albumin) held, which alone would be same. Scored contra because rats and monkeys can show oedema and lung injury yet were silent on peripheral oedema and on ILD/pneumonitis (both label warnings), and the in-vitro plus mouse UV-LLNA phototoxicity call produced one grade 1 case in 334. A reviewer who treats the oedema silence as mechanistically unshowable in animals would score this same with partial.

safety.model: Mouse xenograft tolerability; GLP rat (26-week) and beagle dog (39-week) toxicology; pigmented-rat phototoxicity (tepotinib)
safety.note: Tepotinib regressed xenografts with no substantial weight loss over 3 weeks; rat/dog GLP findings not yet public.
safety.short: No weight loss at regression doses
safety.quote: Both drugs were well tolerated and induced no substantial weight loss after more than 3 weeks of treatment.

safety.magnitude_basis: organ-level concordance (lung, liver, oedema, photosensitivity); rat exposures reached only 0.04-0.13x human AUC in the 26-week study
safety.confidence_note: FDA nonclinical executive summary read; the oedema call rests on 'increased weight gain without increased food consumption, suggestive of edema' in a 28-day rat study and periportal oedema in the liver, a weak signal for a 63% clinical incidence.
safety.model: Mouse xenograft tolerability; GLP rat (26-week) and beagle dog (39-week) toxicology; pigmented-rat phototoxicity (tepotinib)
safety.note: Rat lung inflammation/fibrosis, liver toxicity in both species, weight gain suggestive of oedema and a negative in-vivo phototoxicity study all matched the clinic.
safety.short: Rat lung, liver, oedema signals matched clinic
safety.quote: One male in the 135 mg/kg group and 1 female in the 15 mg/kg recovery group had chronic necrotizing lung inflammation; pneumonitis and interstitial lung disease occurs clinically and is included in the warnings section of the label.
safety.reason: Rat and dog toxicology matched tepotinib harms
safety.judgement: Kept on its own track because the species pair (rat/dog) and the findings differ from capmatinib's rat/monkey package; one track would leave the capmatinib contra sticky and hide that tepotinib's animals did flag lung injury and oedema. The 3T3 phototoxicity positive was overturned by the pigmented-rat study and no clinical photosensitivity followed, so that in-vitro-to-in-vivo correction is a match for the animal.
